title: Mississippi man convicted in federal court for child exploitation conspiracy
text:
← Back to the wire
Mississippi man convicted in federal court for child exploitation conspiracy
A federal jury has convicted Justin Lee Plunk on charges related to distributing child sexual abuse material across multiple online platforms over several years. Evidence showed involvement with recruiting minors as young as ten into producing illicit content for profit.
A federal jury in Pittsburgh convicted Justin Lee Plunk, 39, of Corinth, Mississippi, on Oct. 9 of conspiring to distribute and distributing child sexual abuse material for profit over several years using platforms such as Instagram and Telegram.
The conviction followed a four-day trial before United States District Judge Robert J. Colville. Plunk was found guilty on two counts after less than two hours of jury deliberation. United States Attorney Troy Rivetti of the Western District of Pennsylvania said, “Justin Plunk was an active participant in a conspiracy that, for years, preyed upon and sexually exploited children for profit through a variety of online platforms, including popular social media and children’s gaming apps and mobile payment services.” Rivetti added that the verdict holds Plunk responsible for his role in the recruitment and abuse of minors.
Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva for the Justice Department’s Criminal Division said, “Justin Plunk exploited the most vulnerable members of our society to turn a profit. He operated a business that trafficked in horrific images of the sexual exploitation of children both in America and abroad. The verdict in this case sends a strong message that such horrific and depraved conduct will be met with accountability.” FBI Pittsburgh Special Agent in Charge Richard Evanchec said, “This verdict reflects the jury’s clear recognition of the harm caused by those who exploit children for their own profit.”
Evidence presented at trial showed that from at least 2021 to 2024, Plunk participated in an online criminal conspiracy recruiting female minors as young as ten years old from Pennsylvania and elsewhere to create packages containing images and videos depicting child sexual exploitation material. The operation used platforms including Instagram, Snapchat, Telegram, Roblox (for recruitment), Cash App, Venmo, Walmart gift cards, and Roblox gift cards as payment methods.
Plunk received more than $57,000 from these activities via cash transfers and retail store gift cards. He had previously been convicted of enticement of a child for sexual purposes in Mississippi in 2016.
Judge Colville scheduled sentencing for Jan. 26, 2027; each count carries up to twenty years’ imprisonment or a fine up to $250,000 or both. Assistant United States Attorney Heidi Grogan and Trial Attorney Gwendelynn Bills prosecuted the case following an investigation by FBI-Pittsburgh and the Mississippi Attorney General’s Office.
